compatibility.rule: Domains are navigation and grouping metadata only. Existing dimension IDs remain the configuration and persistence units.

domains.description: Defines the overall visual direction and its identity.
Groups appearance mode with palettes and semantic color mapping; theme and color remain independently configurable.
Font families, scale, weights, line heights, tracking and language fallbacks.
Groups spatial scale and information density without merging their token responsibilities.
Geometry, corner radii, border widths, styles and semantic border colors.
The page canvas, material surfaces, elevation and decorative visual effects.
Image direction, image treatment, icon family and icon geometry.
Page composition, grid structure, containers, navigation patterns and responsive behavior.
Reusable interface component structures, variants and component-level styling.
Charts and structured data presentation patterns; must preserve business data semantics.
Behavior and feedback states such as hover, active, focus, disabled, loading and error.
Transitions, timing, easing, animation triggers and reduced-motion behavior.

invariants: Every canonical dimension appears in exactly one domain.
Domain IDs are presentation taxonomy IDs and must not replace canonical dimension IDs.
Resources remain attached to their existing canonical dimension IDs.
A domain selection is a navigation/grouping operation, not an implicit bulk-apply operation.
A style preset may provide defaults across dimensions, but locked dimensions and explicit overrides retain existing composer semantics.
